draft.title: The coefficient of determination
card: The coefficient of determination is r². It is found by squaring the correlation coefficient r.
r² tells us the proportion of the variation in the response variable that is explained by the variation in the explanatory variable. Write it as a percentage by multiplying by 100.
The rest, 1 − r², is not explained by the explanatory variable. It is due to other factors and chance.
Worked example: r = 0.7. Then r² = 0.49, so 49% of the variation in y is explained by x. The other 51% is not.
draft.remember: r² is the percentage of variation in y explained by x.

a.q: A data set has r = 0.9. What percentage of the variation in y is explained by x?
a.why: r² = 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, so 81% is explained. Giving 90% mistakes r for r². The value 19% is the part not explained.
a.clue: Square r before turning it into a percentage.

b.q: For a sample of cafés, r² = 0.36 between daily visitors and sales, and the trend is negative. What is r, and what percentage is not explained by visitors?
b.why: r = −√0.36 = −0.6, with the sign matching the negative trend. The unexplained part is 1 − 0.36 = 0.64, or 64%. The 36% is the explained part.
b.clue: Take the square root, then check the direction of the trend.

problems.detail: A negative trend between daily café visitors and sales is implausible, since more visitors would normally mean more sales. This could confuse students. A context where a negative association makes sense would be better, such as price and number sold.

check.summary: The card, both answers and the explanations are correct. The only issue is that question b uses an implausible negative link between café visitors and sales, which should be swapped for a context where a negative trend makes sense.

proposal.title: The coefficient of determination
card: The coefficient of determination is r². It is found by squaring the correlation coefficient r, so it is always between 0 and 1.

r² is the proportion of the variation in the response variable explained by the variation in the explanatory variable. Multiply by 100 to write it as a percentage. The rest, 1 − r², is due to other factors.
To go back from r² to r, take the square root. Give r the sign of the association: negative if y tends to fall as x rises.
Worked example: r = −0.7. Then r² = 0.49, so 49% of the variation in y is explained by x. The other 51% is not.
proposal.remember: Square r to find the share of variation in y explained by x. The rest is not explained.

a.q: A data set has r = 0.9. What percentage of the variation in y is explained by x?
a.why: r² = 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, so 81% is explained. Giving 90% mistakes r for r². The value 19% is the part not explained.
a.clue: Square r before turning it into a percentage.

b.q: For a sample of bakeries, r² = 0.36 between the price of a loaf and loaves sold each day. The association is negative. What is r, and what percentage is not explained by price?
b.why: r = −√0.36 = −0.6, negative because sales fall as price rises. The unexplained part is 1 − 0.36 = 0.64, or 64%. The 36% is the explained part, not the unexplained part.
b.clue: Take the square root, then check the direction of the association.
